global_caption: The video contains 5 shots and is a cool blue anime-style space origami tutorial. The overall color tone is consistently futuristic cool blue and silver white. The camera movement is gentle and flowing, conveying a sense of weightlessness and floating. The Lighting is primarily composed of cold natural light streaming through the viewport and soft ambient lighting within the spacecraft cabin.
shot1: The first shot begins with a fade-in, presenting a wide overhead view with slight pan of the zero-gravity spacecraft observation cabin. A silver-blue square paper floats in the foreground, while a completed starbird crane hovers nearby as a reference model. In the background, a curved viewport reveals slowly drifting starfields.
shot2: The second shot connects to the previous shot with a hard cut, transitioning to an overhead close-up. The camera remains stable above the worktable, centered on the silver-blue square paper. Hands enter from both sides of the frame. The foreground shows only hands and paper, while the background blurs into cool blue cabin walls and floating small objects. Shallow depth of field makes the fold lines extremely clear. The astronaut first folds the square diagonally into a triangle, then folds it again to create a central crease. As fingertips press along the edge, subtle changes in paper reflection are visible. Auxiliary lighting evenly illuminates the creases. The camera slightly lowers and performs a very gentle follow pan, ensuring precise and easy-to-follow step demonstration.
shot3: The third shot transitions from the previous shot with a brief hard cut into a hand extreme close-up. The camera is slightly overhead and eye-level, focusing on the central crease of the paper. The foreground shows the unfolded square paper, while the background is completely blurred into cool-colored bokeh. The paper gradually transforms from flat to a neat diamond shape. Fingers quickly yet gently smooth the creases. The silver-blue paper sparkles subtly under the cool light like metal. The The camera slightly pushes in, further emphasizing alignment of corners and formation of creases.
shot4: The fourth shot transitions from the previous shot via a smooth action match to a medium-close eye-level angle. The upper body of the character re-enters the frame. The background reveals the curved structure of the observation cabin and floating instrument lights. Foreground, midground, and background are clearly layered: the foreground shows the diamond-shaped paper held in her palm, the midground shows her focused face and hands working together, and the background features the cool blue viewport light band. The astronaut performs reverse inward folds to form the head and tail of the paper crane, then gently spreads the wings outward. The movements are fluid and clear, transforming the compact angular shape into a three-dimensional bird-like structure. Lighting remains primarily cold natural light, with only soft highlights outlining the paper edges. The camera uses a slow, small-scale orbital pan to emphasize the transformation from flat to three-dimensional.
shot5: The fifth shot transitions from the previous shot with a fade-in/fade-out effect to a close-up in front of the viewport. The camera is slightly low-angle, focusing on the completed starbird crane held in her palm. The foreground shows the clear outline of her hand and the crane, the midground shows her satisfied and gentle expression, and the background features the deep blue starfield and distant nebulae. The composition places the crane in front of the bright area of the viewport, creating a distinct silhouette and metallic reflection. She gently releases her fingers, allowing the crane to float slowly toward the window in zero gravity. The wings flutter slightly in minor air currents. The final product is fully displayed. The camera slowly pulls out, concluding the tutorial naturally with the completed artwork and poetic space imagery.
